newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Feb spot natgas notionally lower on weather.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Feb spot natgas notionally lower on weather.

text.p: U.S. spot natgas prices for February delivery were notionally lower Thursday, pressured by forecasts calling for more moderate weather next week, sources said.
Feb 1 prices on the Gulf Coast pipes were talked mostly in the $2.80-2.85 per million British thermal units range, but no deals were confirmed done since nomination deadlines had already expired.
Gulf Coast prices for the remaining day of January were mostly steady around $3.
In south Texas, February prices were also talked slightly lower in the high-$2.60s to low-$2.70s.
In the Midcontinent, February prices were notionally flat in the $2.70-2.75 range, while prices for Friday slid 20-25 cents to the $2.65-2.70 range.
In west Texas, Permian prices for Feb 1 fell about five cents to the $2.50-2.55 range. Prices for Friday were also softer in the mid-$2.60s.
February prices at the southern California border were talked about three cents lower around $2.60 as above-normal temperatures blanketed most of the Southwest.
In the East, February prices at the New York city-gate were notionally at $3.50-3.60, falling more than a $1 from January indices.
